state.task:
Question-answering task over a company handbook.

The handbook is in /task/fixtures/handbook/ (40 documents, HB-01.md to HB-40.md). Each document
has a header line (version, status, effective dates, what it supersedes) and numbered sections;
each section is a passage, cited as "HB-07 §2". Documents can have superseded versions, and
memos can add group exceptions and carve-outs. Use the rule that applies to the situation and
date in the question.

Tools (in your code):
  import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/task/fixtures")
  from handbook_tools import search, show
  search("lodging limit Geneva", k=5)   # up to k (at most 8) ranked passages, with ids
  show(["HB-07 §2", "HB-12 §3"])        # the named passages in full
Every search result is also saved under /task/workspace/search-results/ (the path is printed in
the result header). You may also read the documents directly.

Questions:
- Q1: What is the daily meal allowance for a standard travel day with an approved client dinner today? (answer in EUR per day)
- Q2: What is the relocation lump sum for an employee relocating to another country in their third month of employment today? (answer in EUR)
- Q3: What is the home-office equipment allowance for an employee with a medical accessibility plan today? (answer in EUR)
- Q4: What mileage rate applied to a business trip in a private petrol car on 2026-04-15? (answer in cents per km)
- Q5: What is the nightly lodging limit for a standard business trip today (2026-10-13)? (answer in EUR per night)
- Q6: What is the purchase approval threshold for a regular department's purchase from a supplier with a framework contract today? (answer in EUR)

Finish with {"action": "final", "answer": {"answers": [{"question": "Q1", "value": "...",
"citations": ["HB-07 §2", ...]}, ...]}}. Give one entry per question. The value must be the
exact amount; citations must include every passage needed to support it (for example the
rule and any exception or carve-out that applies), not just one passage.
state.step_intent: Find the mileage rate that applies to: What mileage rate applied to a business trip in a private petrol car on 2026-04-15?

passages.source: HB-11 §4 | Policy FAQ — Current mileage rate | version: 7 · status: current · effective: 2026-01-15
passages.text: Q: What is the current standard mileage rate? A: 28 cents per km, as set in HB-36 §2 (effective 2026-05-01). Group exceptions are listed in HB-31.

passages.source: HB-31 §1 | Memo: mileage rate exceptions — Purpose | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-04-01
passages.text: This memo lists group exceptions to the mileage rate in HB-36. Repeated late or incomplete claims may be escalated to the head of the department. Where a local agreement sets stricter rules, the stricter rule applies for that location. Receipts must be attached for every item claimed; photographs of paper receipts are accepted.

passages.source: HB-31 §2 | Memo: mileage rate exceptions — Exception for electric vehicles | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-04-01
passages.text: For electric vehicles, the mileage rate is 44 cents per km instead of the standard amount. Employees should keep costs reasonable and book through the approved channels where possible. Audit samples are drawn every quarter, and selected employees are asked for documentation. Repeated late or incomplete claims may be escalated to the head of the department.

passages.source: HB-31 §3 | Memo: mileage rate exceptions — Carve-out | version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-04-01
passages.text: The exception above does not apply to electric rental cars; they follow the standard mileage rate in HB-36 §2. Questions about this section go to the policy owner named in the document header. The policy owner may publish clarifications in the policy FAQ without changing this section. Supporting records are kept for seven years in line with the retention schedule.

passages.source: HB-36 §5 | Travel policy: private car use — Exceptions | version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-05-01 · supersedes: HB-27
passages.text: Group exceptions to the mileage rate are published in HB-31. Amounts are stated in euros; conversions use the published rate on the day of payment. This section is reviewed once a year by the finance team together with the policy owner. Line managers check each claim for plausibility before it is released for payment.
